priorityStack.title: Mission Control v1 handoff readiness
priorityStack.summary: Core specs, reference UI, data contract, and handoff materials are now in place for outside coders.
priorityStack.nextAction: Hand off the package and review their first pass for drift from the executive model

priorityStack.title: Startup / relaunch hardening
priorityStack.summary: Startup flow still needs the dedicated tmux session, stale-window cleanup, and morning checklist wiring requested earlier.
priorityStack.nextAction: Implement the startup improvements in a lean, non-brittle way

decisionQueue.decision: External build style for Mission Control
decisionQueue.whyItMatters: A heavy app stack too early creates maintenance drag and slows iteration before the information model is proven.
decisionQueue.recommendation: Static-first or very lightweight framework only

decisionQueue.decision: First real data sections to prioritize
decisionQueue.whyItMatters: Attempting to fully populate everything at once will create noise and low-value busywork.
decisionQueue.recommendation: Priorities + decision queue first, then ops health, then cost watch

nodes.label: Owner
nodes.summary: Final decision-maker. Sets priorities, approves major tradeoffs, and defines acceptable risk.

nodes.label: Saidee
nodes.summary: CEO / operator. Translates goals into execution, surfaces risks, and maintains operating discipline.

nodes.label: CFO
nodes.summary: Financial control, spend visibility, vendor scrutiny, and ROI discipline.
nodes.activationTrigger: Recurring spend needs regular review, vendor governance grows, or budget drift lacks ownership

nodes.label: CTO / Infrastructure
nodes.summary: Keep systems reliable, secure, maintainable, and automation-friendly.
nodes.activationTrigger: Infrastructure work becomes continuous, reliability/security issues recur, or tooling debt starts accumulating

nodes.label: Chief of Staff
nodes.summary: Reduce coordination drag, keep follow-through tight, and organize priorities.
nodes.activationTrigger: Follow-ups slip, planning/admin overhead becomes a bottleneck, or project coordination debt rises

nodes.label: Research / Intelligence
nodes.summary: Monitor changes and produce decision-useful analysis.
nodes.activationTrigger: Recurring monitoring becomes valuable or strategic decisions need regular analysis support

nodes.label: Operations
nodes.summary: Day-to-day operational hygiene, maintenance cadence, and routine execution.
nodes.activationTrigger: Recurring operational tasks create drag or maintenance work needs explicit ownership

nodes.label: Communications
nodes.summary: Manage outbound obligations, follow-ups, and message discipline.
nodes.activationTrigger: External communication load increases or follow-up obligations become easy to miss

opsHealth.name: Saidee startup and relaunch flow
opsHealth.issue: Still needs dedicated tmux session handling and stale TUI window cleanup before relaunch.
opsHealth.recommendedNextStep: Implement the hardening pass with reliability favored over cleverness

opsHealth.name: Morning bootstrap / startup checklist
opsHealth.issue: Checklist is requested conceptually but not yet wired into the startup flow.
opsHealth.recommendedNextStep: Add a short morning checklist and keep it intentionally small

opsHealth.name: Dashboard specs and reference build
opsHealth.recommendedNextStep: Use it for external builder handoff and review for drift after first implementation

costWatch.name: Dashboard implementation complexity
costWatch.utilizationNote: Value comes from clarity and fast scanning, not engineering weight.
costWatch.actionRecommendation: Keep the first pass static or lightweight until the information model is stable

costWatch.name: Premature automation
costWatch.baseline: Risk rises if unstable or low-value sources are automated too early
costWatch.utilizationNote: Manual high-signal inputs are currently more valuable than noisy automation.
costWatch.actionRecommendation: Automate only after recurring manual pain is obvious
